chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Yunus and Ali al-Sayrafī, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If I am by the side of the road and the time for Maghrib prayer arrives while I intend to go to my home, if I delay the prayer until I pray at home, it will be easier for me and I will catch the evening. Should I then pray in some of the mosques?' He said, 'Pray at your home.'

key_terms.الْمِصْرِ: The road or side of the road

ai.seo_question: Should a traveler delay Maghrib prayer to pray at home instead of in the mosque?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a traveler or individual away from home may delay Maghrib to pray at their residence for ease, explicitly preferring the home over the mosque in this specific context of convenience. This ruling highlights the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding the location of prayer, prioritizing the ease of the worshipper (*rukhsa*) when circumstances such as travel or distance make the mosque less practical, while maintaining the validity of the prayer within its prescribed time.
